title: Design System: Alex Mudge — Data & Insights Lead

name.purpose: The NAME field value — the one outsized element on the page, sized as the biggest grid field, not a hero headline.

heading.purpose: SUMMARY / CAPABILITIES / ATTACHED EXHIBITS / AUTHORIZED CONTACT — no decorative numbering prefix.

body.purpose: The summary paragraph; the only long-form prose on the page.

field.purpose: Every filled-in data point: ref no., role, location, dates, tags, reference codes.

label.purpose: The small caption above every field value.

shadows.name: stacked-sheet
shadows.purpose: Applied once to the record's ::before pseudo-element, simulating a real sheet beneath it. The system's only shadow.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: The status stamp's one-time press-in on load — the system's single authored motion moment.

motion.name: section-reveal
motion.purpose: Quiet, supporting scroll reveal for each record section; deliberately not the same device as the stamp press.

components.name: Status Stamp
components.description: Rubber-stamp status mark with a one-time press-in animation.
components.css: .ds-stamp { display: inline-block; border: 2px solid #a3242f; color: #a3242f; font-family: 'Courier Prime', monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; transform: rotate(-3deg); }

components.name: Field Grid Item
components.description: Label-above-value pairing used throughout the record header and fields.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; font-family: 'Courier Prime', monospace; font-size: 0.63rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #576573; margin-bottom: 0.3rem; } .ds-field-value { font-family: 'Courier Prime', monospace; font-size: 0.95rem; color: #1c2530; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Exhibit Card
components.description: Filed project card with a tab label, staple mark, and functional cross-reference footer.

narrative.overview:
The site is one professional record, not a portfolio grid. It reads like an institutional personnel/records-office document: a bordered record card holds identity and career facts in a real field grid, career history sits in a service-record table, capabilities read as a signed-off competency checklist, and project work is filed underneath as numbered, staple-marked exhibits — evidence attached to the record, not the record itself.

This is a deliberate replacement of an earlier dark, neon-cyan, terminal/hacker-console identity, made on the explicit direction to remove that look entirely. Depth comes from real stacked-paper offset, never colored glow or blur. Color is restrained to two neutral inks plus exactly one accent — a stamp-red reserved for status and proof — never ambient branding or category color-coding.
keyCharacteristics: One record-card shell, not a multi-hero portfolio layout; project work is explicitly subordinate, filed as exhibits
Restrained palette: two neutral inks + one stamp-red accent used only for status/proof, never ambient
Serif for the record's own prose, monospace exclusively for typed/filled data fields
Depth from real stacked-paper offset and hairline rules; no glow, no blur-as-decoration, no gradients
Cross-reference codes (exhibit ↔ capability) are functional, not decorative section numbering

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Stamp-red is spent only on status and proof — never on ambient decoration, never split across categories.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from stacked-paper offset shadows and rule-line opacity, never colored glow, backdrop blur, or gradients.

rules.name: The Typed-vs-Set Rule
rules.body: Text the document 'printed' is Source Serif 4; text that reads as 'filled in' is Courier Prime. Mixing the two within a role is a defect.

rules.name: The Stacked-Paper Rule
rules.body: Depth is a physical fact — real paper sheets under the top one — not a floating-card effect. One shadow instance in the whole system.

dos: Do keep Courier Prime exclusively for typed/filled data and Source Serif 4 exclusively for the record's own prose.
Do spend stamp-red only on status, proof, and the one primary action.
Do build depth from real stacked-paper offset and rule-line opacity, never glow or gradient.
Do mark unfilled/future content honestly with a labeled 'pending' exhibit rather than fabricating it.
Do keep cross-reference codes functional (real anchor links), not decorative section numbering.
donts: Don't reintroduce the previous dark/neon-cyan/terminal-console identity, gradients, glow, or particle-canvas motion.
Don't add rounded corners; every shape is a hard rectangle except the deliberately rotated stamps.
Don't color-code categories with multiple accent hues.
Don't use a Unicode glyph or emoji as an icon.
Don't add a decorative section-number sequence that carries no cross-referencable information.
